hints: Look closely at the words 'each individual' in B and C versus 'different' in D. Ask yourself, can a bulk solution physically flow two opposite ways inside one tiny tube at the same moment?

Remember what drives long distance movement in phloem: a pressure gradient from source to sink. Active transport is only for loading and unloading, so one tube can only have one pressure direction at a time.
walkthrough:
**Recall how substances really travel in phloem**

Think of phloem transport as bulk flow, not individual molecules swimming. Sucrose and amino acids are carried together in solution by mass flow from a source to a sink.

Key rule: mass flow = bulk movement down a hydrostatic pressure gradient.

**See why one tube can only flow one way**

A single sieve tube element has high pressure at one end (where sugars are loaded) and low pressure at the other end (where they are removed). Water follows by osmosis and pushes the whole sap along.

That means one tube, one gradient, one direction at a time. Opposite flows in the same tube would cancel out.

**Explain movement in different directions**

A stem contains many separate sieve tubes bundled together. At the same time, one tube can have a source to sink gradient pointing up, while a neighbouring tube has a different source to sink gradient pointing down.

So sucrose might go leaf to root in one tube, while amino acids go in the opposite direction in a different tube. That is exactly option D.

options.A: Active transport does not carry sap along the sieve tube. It is only used for loading at the source and unloading at the sink, while long distance movement is always by mass flow.
options.B: Long distance transport in a sieve tube is by mass flow only. Active transport does not occur along the length of the tube to move sap.
options.C: Mass flow in opposite directions cannot happen in the same tube at the same time, as a tube can only have one pressure gradient and therefore one flow direction.
options.D: This is correct. Different sieve tubes are independent, so each can have its own source to sink pressure gradient and carry mass flow in a different direction at the same time.
